# entropy_src_core Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Overview

The `entropy_src_core` module is the central entropy-processing engine for the entropy source IP. It receives raw entropy samples from an external noise source, performs online health testing, optionally conditions the entropy, buffers the resulting seeds, and delivers them either to a hardware consumer or to software through the register interface.

The module must:

- Collect raw entropy samples only while enabled.
- Perform continuous health testing on the raw entropy stream.
- Provide both normal conditioned entropy and a bypass path for boot-time or software-selected operation.
- Support firmware override operation, including observing raw entropy and injecting firmware-processed entropy.
- Deliver 384-bit entropy seeds together with a FIPS-compliance indication.
- Generate interrupts, recoverable alerts, and fatal alerts for the appropriate events.
- Detect and report internal datapath, FIFO, counter, and conditioner errors.

## 2. Operating Modes

### 2.1 Disabled Mode

When the module is disabled:

- The external RNG interface must be deasserted.
- Incoming RNG data must be ignored.
- All internal entropy FIFOs and packing buffers must be cleared.
- Health testing must be inactive.
- No entropy seeds may be produced.
- Internal state machines must return to idle.

### 2.2 Enabled Mode

When the module is enabled, it shall continuously receive raw entropy samples, process them through health testing and conditioning or bypass, and make the resulting seeds available for consumption.

### 2.3 Boot-Time Bypass Mode

After reset, the module must start in boot-time bypass mode.

In bypass mode:

- Raw entropy is health-tested using the bypass health-test window and bypass thresholds.
- The entropy is not passed through the cryptographic conditioner.
- The FIPS-compliance flag must not be asserted for entropy delivered from this mode.

The module shall exit boot-time bypass mode after the initial boot sequence and enter normal conditioned operation, unless software has explicitly selected the bypass path.

### 2.4 Normal FIPS Mode

In normal FIPS mode:

- Raw entropy is health-tested using the normal health-test window and normal thresholds.
- Health-tested entropy is passed through the cryptographic conditioner to produce 384-bit full-entropy seeds.
- The FIPS-compliance flag must be asserted for seeds produced by this path, provided the full RNG bus is used and bit-selection mode is disabled.

### 2.5 Software-Selected Bypass Mode

If software selects the bypass entropy type, the module must continue to operate in bypass mode even after the boot-time phase has completed. This allows software to perform its own conditioning or to read raw entropy through the software path.

### 2.6 Firmware Override Mode

Firmware override mode allows software to take control of the entropy path:

- Raw post-health-test entropy can be captured into an observe FIFO and read by software.
- Software can optionally insert entropy back into the pipeline to be conditioned or bypassed.
- Firmware override mode must only be active when both the firmware override control field is valid and a fuse-provided override enable is asserted.

## 3. Configuration and Security Behavior

### 3.1 Multi-Bit Control Fields

Security-sensitive configuration fields are multi-bit encoded. The module must recognize valid True and False encodings.

If an invalid encoding is written to any such field:

- The module must treat the field as False.
- The module must assert a recoverable alert.
- The corresponding recoverable alert status must be set.

This applies to enable, entropy data register enable, firmware override mode, firmware override entropy insertion, RNG bit enable, entropy route, entropy type, boot bypass disable, and health-test clear controls.

### 3.2 Fuse-Gated Functions

The module must support independent fuse-provided enables for:

- The software entropy register read path.
- The firmware override mode.

If the relevant fuse enable is not asserted, register reads or writes associated with that function must have no effect on the entropy datapath.

### 3.3 Boot Bypass Disable

If boot bypass disable is configured, the module must leave boot-time bypass mode once enabled and must not use the boot bypass path. The module may still use bypass mode if software explicitly selects the bypass entropy type.

### 3.4 Alert Threshold Configuration

The alert threshold is protected by an inverted companion field. If the threshold and its inverted companion do not match, the module must assert a recoverable configuration alert.

The alert threshold determines how many health-test failure events must occur before a recoverable alert is raised. A threshold of zero must disable alert generation from this source.

## 4. RNG Input and Preprocessing

### 4.1 Raw Sample Capture

The module receives 4-bit raw entropy samples from the external RNG. When enabled, each valid sample must be captured into the input path.

If the module is disabled, RNG valid assertions must be ignored and the input path must be cleared.

### 4.2 Bit-Selection Mode

The module may operate in either full-bus mode or bit-selection mode:

- In full-bus mode, all 4 bits of each RNG sample are used.
- In bit-selection mode, one of the 4 bit lanes is selected, and the selected bit stream is packed into 4-bit symbols for downstream processing.

When bit-selection mode is enabled, the module must not assert the FIPS-compliance flag on generated entropy seeds.

### 4.3 Bypass Indication to RNG

The module must provide a bypass-mode indication to the external RNG. This indication must be asserted whenever the module is operating in bypass mode. This allows the RNG to adjust its behavior if desired.

## 5. Health Testing

### 5.1 General Behavior

While enabled, the module must continuously run health checks on the raw entropy stream.

Health tests must be inactive while the module is disabled.

A health-test clear operation must:

- Reset all health-test counters.
- Reset all health-test watermark registers.
- Reset all health-test fail counters.
- Reset the common window counter.

### 5.2 Health-Test Window

The module must maintain a common window counter that advances with each valid entropy sample.

The window length must be selectable between:

- A bypass-mode window, used during boot-time or software-selected bypass operation.
- A normal FIPS-mode window, used during normal conditioned operation.

When the window counter reaches the selected window length, the module must generate a window-done event. The window-done event is used by the window-based health tests to evaluate counts over the completed window.

### 5.3 Required Health Tests

The module must implement the following internal health tests:

- Repetition count test, to detect repeated identical samples.
- Repetition count symbol test, to detect repeated symbols.
- Adaptive proportion test, to detect bias in the number of high or low values.
- Bucket test, to detect bias in symbol distribution.
- Markov test, to detect unexpected first-order temporal correlations.

Each test must:

- Observe the raw entropy samples and valid indication.
- Compare its measured statistic against the selected threshold.
- Generate a fail pulse when the threshold is exceeded.
- Update its running total-fail counter.
- Update the appropriate high or low watermark register.

### 5.4 Threshold Selection

Each health test must have separate thresholds for bypass mode and normal FIPS mode. The module must automatically select the threshold corresponding to the current mode.

Threshold register writes must be monotonic in the direction that preserves or increases the strictness of the test. A write that would weaken the configured threshold must not take effect.

### 5.5 Health-Test Failures

If any internal health test detects a failure, the module must:

- Increment the fail counter for that test.
- Increment the aggregate health-test fail counter.
- Set a health-test-failed condition used for alert and interrupt generation.

### 5.6 External Health Test Interface

The module must provide an external health-test interface. Through this interface, the module must make the raw entropy samples, valid indication, clear signal, active indication, high threshold, low threshold, and window length available to an external test block.

The module must accept from the external block:

- A measured test count.
- A high-threshold fail pulse.
- A low-threshold fail pulse.

External health-test results must be incorporated into the same watermark, fail-counter, and alert infrastructure as the internal health tests.

### 5.7 Health-Test Alert Summary

When the aggregate health-test fail counter reaches the configured alert threshold, the module must assert a recoverable alert.

The module must also expose per-test fail counts and total fail counts for software visibility.

## 6. Entropy Conditioning and Data Path

### 6.1 Post-Health-Test Packing

After health testing, the raw entropy samples must be packed into wider words for the conditioning stage.

The packing process must be cleared when the module is disabled.

### 6.2 Normal Conditioned Path

In normal FIPS mode, packed health-tested entropy must be fed into the cryptographic conditioner.

The conditioner must:

- Accept 64-bit message words.
- Accumulate them until enough data has been received.
- Produce a 384-bit conditioned entropy seed.

The module must not present additional message words to the conditioner while the conditioner input is not ready.

If the conditioner shares an external cryptographic engine with another block, the module must be able to request exclusive use of that engine and must not push data until the request is acknowledged.

### 6.3 Bypass Path

In bypass mode, packed health-tested entropy must not be sent through the conditioner. Instead, the module must pack the data directly into 384-bit seeds.

The bypass path must be cleared when the module is disabled.

### 6.4 Final Entropy FIFO

All completed 384-bit seeds, whether conditioned or bypassed, must be stored in a final entropy FIFO together with their FIPS-compliance flag.

The final FIFO must be cleared when the module is disabled.

The current fill level of the final FIFO must be observable by software for debug and status purposes.

### 6.5 FIPS-Compliance Flag

Each stored seed must carry a FIPS-compliance flag.

The flag must be asserted only when all of the following are true:

- The module is enabled.
- The seed was produced by the normal conditioned path, not the bypass path.
- The full 4-bit RNG bus is being used.
- Bit-selection mode is disabled.

In all other cases, the FIPS-compliance flag must be deasserted.

### 6.6 Data-Integrity Monitoring

The module must monitor entropy words as they leave the final FIFO.

If two consecutive words have the same lower 64-bit portion, the module must assert a recoverable alert. This is a tamper-detection countermeasure.

## 7. Entropy Output and Distribution

### 7.1 Hardware Entropy Interface

The module must provide a hardware interface for delivering 384-bit entropy seeds to downstream hardware consumers.

When a consumer requests a seed and a seed is available in the final FIFO:

- The module must acknowledge the request.
- The module must present the full 384-bit seed.
- The module must present the associated FIPS-compliance flag.

If no seed is available, the request must remain pending until a seed becomes available.

When software routing is selected, the hardware interface must not consume seeds from the final FIFO. Seeds are instead routed to the software read path.

### 7.2 Software Entropy Read Path

When software routing is selected, final entropy seeds must be moved from the final FIFO into a software-readable unpacking FIFO.

The module must present the entropy to software as 32-bit words. Reading the entropy data register must pop one 32-bit word from the unpacking FIFO.

A complete 384-bit seed is consumed over 12 reads.

The software read path must be gated by:

- A fuse-provided software register enable.
- A valid entropy data register enable field.

If either gate is not asserted, reads must not pop the entropy FIFO and must return zero.

### 7.3 Entropy Available Indication

The module must generate an entropy-available event whenever the software entropy read FIFO is non-empty. This event must be used for the entropy-valid interrupt.

## 8. Firmware Override Data Path

### 8.1 Observe FIFO

When firmware override mode is active, post-health-test packed entropy must be captured into an observe FIFO.

The observe FIFO must:

- Be 64 entries deep.
- Store 32-bit words.
- Be readable by software through a dedicated read register.
- Expose its current depth to software.
- Be cleared when the module is disabled.

The observe FIFO must be prevented from overflowing. If software does not drain it, older entries must be discarded as needed to keep the datapath operational.

### 8.2 Observe FIFO Threshold and Interrupt

A software-programmable threshold must be compared against the observe FIFO depth.

When firmware override mode is active and the depth reaches the threshold, the module must assert the observe-FIFO-ready event.

### 8.3 Firmware Entropy Insertion

When firmware override mode and firmware entropy insertion are active, software-written 32-bit words must be injected into the pre-conditioner packing stage in place of the normal post-health-test data.

The injected data must then follow the selected normal or bypass path just like hardware-generated entropy.

This feature allows software to perform its own health testing or conditioning and reinject the processed entropy into the pipeline.

Firmware entropy insertion must only be active if the firmware override control field is valid and the fuse-provided override enable is asserted.

## 9. Interrupts

The module must generate the following interrupt events:

- **Entropy valid:** asserted when at least one 32-bit word is available in the software entropy read path.
- **Health test failed:** asserted when a health-test failure is escalated by the main control logic.
- **Observe FIFO ready:** asserted when the observe FIFO depth reaches its programmed threshold in firmware override mode.
- **Fatal error:** asserted when a fatal internal error condition is detected.

Interrupts must follow the standard enable, status, and test register behavior. Writing to the interrupt test register must cause the corresponding interrupt to be asserted. The interrupt state must be observable by software and clearable through the interrupt state register.

## 10. Alerts

### 10.1 Recoverable Alerts

The module must assert a recoverable alert for any of the following conditions:

- An invalid multi-bit configuration field is detected.
- A health-test alert threshold has been reached.
- A health-test failure is escalated by the main control logic.
- A data-integrity monitor detects repeated identical entropy words.
- The alert threshold and its inverted companion are inconsistent.

### 10.2 Fatal Alerts

The module must assert a fatal alert for any of the following conditions:

- An internal FIFO error is detected.
- An internal control state machine error is detected.
- A counter replication error is detected.
- The cryptographic conditioner reports an error.
- A fatal error is forced through the error injection interface.

### 10.3 Alert Test Interface

The module must provide alert test inputs. When software asserts an alert test request, the corresponding alert output must be pulsed. Alert test requests must not otherwise change functional behavior.

## 11. Error Detection and Reporting

### 11.1 FIFO Errors

The module must detect and report the following FIFO error classes:

- A push attempt while the FIFO is full.
- A pop attempt while the FIFO is empty.
- A FIFO status inconsistency, such as full and empty being asserted simultaneously.

Any FIFO error must set the corresponding error status bit and contribute to the fatal alert and fatal-error interrupt.

### 11.2 State Machine Errors

The module must detect illegal transitions or assertions from its internal control state machines. Such errors must be reported as fatal errors.

### 11.3 Counter Errors

The module uses replicated counters for security-sensitive counting. If replicated counter values disagree, the module must report a counter error and treat it as a fatal error.

### 11.4 Conditioner Errors

If the cryptographic conditioner reports an error or enters an illegal state, the module must report it as a fatal error and assert the fatal alert.

### 11.5 Error Status Registers

Error status bits, once set, must remain set until cleared by software.

The module must also provide error source and error type status fields so software can distinguish between:

- FIFO write errors.
- FIFO read errors.
- FIFO state errors.
- Control state machine errors.
- Counter errors.

### 11.6 Error Injection

The module must support software error injection for verification and diagnostics.

When a specific error is injected through the error injection register, the module must report it in the same way as a real error, including setting status bits and asserting the appropriate fatal alert and interrupt.

## 12. Debug and Status Visibility

The module must provide debug status information, including:

- The fill level of the final entropy FIFO.
- The state of the conditioner engine.
- The idle state of the main control logic.
- Any conditioner error status.

Debug status fields must be read-only and must not affect functional behavior.

# entropy_src_main_sm Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is the main control state machine for the entropy source datapath. It decides when health-test results are accepted, when boot-time samples are discarded or forwarded, when the conditioning engine is started and processed, and when alert or error behavior must be entered.

The module does not compute or transform entropy data. It only observes status/control indications and produces the control actions needed to move data through the entropy pipeline in the correct order.

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

After reset, the module must be in its idle state.

In the idle state:

- The module must assert the idle status indication.
- All data-transfer, conditioning, alert, error, and power-coordination outputs must be deasserted.
- The module must remain idle until the enable input is asserted.

When the module is enabled from idle:

- If boot/bypass mode is selected, it must enter the boot-time phase.
- Otherwise, it must enter the startup qualification phase.

## 3. Enable and Disable Behavior

The enable input controls whether the module is allowed to process entropy.

The module must behave as follows when disabled:

- If disabled while in the idle state, it must remain idle.
- If disabled during the boot-time phase or during startup qualification before the conditioning sequence begins, it must return to idle immediately.
- If disabled at the beginning of a continuous health-test cycle, before the health-test wait has started, it must return to idle immediately.
- If disabled while a continuous health-test result is being awaited, it must not stop abruptly. It must proceed through the current conditioning completion sequence and return to idle only after the conditioning done indication has been generated.
- If disabled while the conditioning completion sequence is already in progress, it must finish that sequence, generate the conditioning done indication, and then return to idle.
- If disabled while waiting for the main entropy output path to accept a completed conditioned sample, the module must generate the conditioning done indication and return to idle without pushing the sample.
- If disabled while in the alert-hang state, it must return to idle.
- If disabled while in the error state, it must remain in the error state until reset.

## 4. Boot-Time Phase

Boot-time mode is the low-latency entropy path used before normal FIPS/CC startup operation begins.

While in the boot-time phase, the module must wait for a health-test result.

During this wait:

- If the boot-time path indicates that a pending sample is available, the module must discard it by issuing a pop to the boot-time path. This prevents a previously failed boot-time sample from being forwarded later.

When a boot-time health-test result completes:

- If the result is a pass, the module must wait until the boot-time sample is available in the boot-time path. Once available, it must:
  - clear the alert failure tally,
  - clear boot/bypass mode so subsequent operation uses the normal path,
  - pop the boot-time sample,
  - push the boot-time sample to the primary entropy output path,
  - enter the startup qualification phase.
- If the result is a fail and the alert-threshold condition is not asserted, the module must return to idle. If the module is still enabled, this may cause the boot-time phase to be attempted again.
- If the result is a fail and the alert-threshold condition is asserted, the module must enter the alert state.

If the module is disabled during the boot-time phase, it must return to idle immediately.

## 5. Startup Qualification Phase

After boot-time mode has completed, or when the module is enabled directly into normal mode, it must perform startup qualification.

At the start of the startup qualification phase:

- If the final entropy storage is full, the module must not begin a new startup cycle. It must return to idle and wait until storage is available and the module is enabled.
- If the module is disabled, it must return to idle.
- If boot/bypass mode is requested at the startup entry point, the module must enter the boot-time phase instead.
- Otherwise, the module must issue a start pulse to the conditioning engine and then wait for health-test results.

The startup qualification must track the sequence of pass/fail health-test results:

- A passing health-test result increments the current run of consecutive passes.
- A failing health-test result resets that run to zero.
- If two consecutive health-test results are failures, the module must enter the alert state.
- When the run of consecutive passes reaches two, startup qualification is complete, and the module must proceed to the conditioning completion sequence.

If the module is disabled during startup qualification, it must return to idle immediately. A full final-entropy-storage condition only affects the start of the startup cycle; once the cycle has begun, it does not abort the qualification.

## 6. Conditioning Completion Sequence

Once startup qualification has completed, or once a continuous health-test result is available, the module must perform the conditioning completion sequence.

The sequence must behave as follows:

1. The module must request the power-coordination handshake and wait for the acknowledge indication before proceeding.
2. The power-coordination request must remain asserted while the conditioning computation is being initiated and while waiting for the conditioning result to become valid.
3. When the acknowledge is received, the module must:
   - clear the alert failure tally,
   - issue the conditioner process pulse.
4. The module must wait until the conditioning engine indicates that its result is valid.
5. When the result is valid:
   - If the module is disabled, it must generate the conditioner done indication and return to idle. It must not push the result to the primary entropy output path.
   - If the primary entropy output path is ready, the module must generate the conditioner done indication and push the result to that path.
   - If the primary entropy output path is not ready, the module must wait until it becomes ready before generating the done indication and pushing the result.

After the conditioned result has been delivered:

- If the module is disabled, it must return to idle.
- If the alert-threshold condition is asserted, it must enter the alert state.
- Otherwise, it must begin the next continuous health-test cycle.

## 7. Continuous Operation

After startup qualification has produced an entropy sample and the module has not been disabled or alerted, the module must enter continuous operation.

A continuous health-test cycle must behave as follows:

- At the start of the cycle:
  - If the final entropy storage is full, the module must not begin the cycle and must return to idle.
  - If the module is disabled, it must return to idle.
  - Otherwise, the module must issue a start pulse to the conditioning engine and then wait for a health-test result.
- When a health-test result is received, both pass and fail results must lead to the conditioning completion sequence. Failing results are counted by the alert-threshold logic and are evaluated after the conditioned output is complete.
- If the module is disabled while waiting for this health-test result, it must proceed into the conditioning completion sequence as part of the graceful shutdown behavior.

After each continuous conditioned output is delivered, the module must check the alert-threshold condition:

- If asserted, enter the alert state.
- Otherwise, begin another continuous health-test cycle.

## 8. Alert Behavior

The module must enter the alert state under any of the following conditions:

- A boot-time health-test fails while the alert-threshold condition is asserted.
- Two consecutive startup health-test results are failures.
- After a conditioned output has been delivered, the alert-threshold condition is asserted.

When the module enters the alert state, it must assert the alert status indication and then move to the alert-hang state.

In the alert-hang state:

- Normal entropy processing and conditioning must be suspended.
- The module must remain in the alert-hang state until the enable input is cleared.
- When the enable input is cleared, the module must return to idle.

## 9. Error Behavior

If the module detects an illegal or invalid internal control state, it must assert the error status indication and remain in the error state.

The module must not automatically recover from the error state. It must remain there until reset.

## 10. Status and Debug Observability

The module must provide status outputs that allow external observation of its current behavior:

- The idle status must be asserted only when the module is in the idle state.
- The alert status must be asserted when the module enters the alert state.
- The error status must be asserted when the module is in the error state.
- A current-state output must reflect the active state of the module, including idle, alert-hang, and error states, for debug and verification purposes.

## 11. Summary of Control Actions

The module must produce the following categories of control action:

- Pop the boot-time path when discarding a failed or stale boot sample, and when forwarding a successful boot sample.
- Push to the primary entropy output path for successful boot-time samples and for completed conditioned samples.
- Start the conditioning engine at the beginning of a startup or continuous health-test cycle.
- Process the conditioning engine only after the power-coordination acknowledge has been received.
- Generate the conditioner done indication when the conditioned result is delivered, and also when the module is disabled during the completion sequence.
- Assert the power-coordination request before processing and hold it until the conditioning result is valid.
- Clear the alert failure tally after a successful boot-time transfer and when initiating the conditioning computation.
- Clear boot/bypass mode after the boot-time sample has been successfully transferred.

The module must not begin new entropy processing when the final entropy storage is full, and it must not deliver new conditioned entropy when the module is disabled or when the primary output path is not ready.
